Field Guide Vision: Unsupervised Structure of Plant-Photo Embeddings

Group meeting update · November 2026

Data: 1,641 BioImages photos, 63 species, 465 individual plants; train / validation / test split by individual plant (1,181 / 249 / 211). Models: EfficientNet-B0, BioCLIP 2.5, DINOv3, YOLO11s (backbone / neck), all frozen. Labels (organ, shot scale, species) are used only to explain and evaluate, never to form the unsupervised groups.

Key findings
  1. 3-D PCA plots lose 13%–32% of organ information; analysis must run in 64-dimensional PCA space
  2. Groupings are most stable and organ-aligned at K = 5–7; about 32% of photos lie between two groups
  3. General vision models group photos by organ; BioCLIP groups them by species
  4. Only EfficientNet concentrates organ information in few dimensions (about 8 per class)
  5. An autoencoder does not improve on PCA; the first principal component is camera distance
  6. Group centres can be shown with real photos; heatmaps are faithful to the model, alignment with organs is untested
  7. Soft clustering shortlists 181 photos that may contain several organs, as candidates for multi-label annotation
  8. Off-the-shelf YOLO embeddings carry the least organ information and need training on organ labels
1 · Which space to analyse in: what dimension reduction keeps

3-D PCA plots lose 13%–32% of organ information; analysis must run in 64-dimensional PCA space

Quantify how much organ, shot-scale and species information each reduction (2-D / 3-D plots, 16 / 64 dimensions) retains, identify the information carried by each principal component, and select the analysis space accordingly.

Line of argument: 1.1 information loss → 1.2 why it is lost → 1.3 consistency across models → 1.4 choice of analysis space → 1.5 display and its use

1.1 Information loss · Information kept after reduction

How information kept is computed: in the reduced space, each photo takes the majority organ (scale, species) of its 5 most similar photos as its guess; the share of correct guesses divided by the same share in the full space; 100% = nothing lost. Result: shot scale survives any reduction; organ information needs about 16 dimensions; species needs 64. In a 3-D plot species information falls to 32% on average.

1.2 Why it is lost · Information carried by EfficientNet's first 6 components (η², 0–1)
PCorganscalespeciesmainly carries

How η² is computed: for each component, photos are grouped by organ (or scale, species), and η² is the share of the component's variation that lies between groups; 1 = the direction is fully determined by that label, 0 = unrelated. Result: the first three components mainly separate organs (PC1 also camera distance); species information is spread over later components, so it is invisible in the first three.

1.5 Display · The same photos drawn three ways (EfficientNet, coloured by organ)

All three maps are computed from the full vectors (1,280-D). In 2-D PCA leaf, inflorescence, fruit and twig overlap; t-SNE and UMAP separate organs, and t-SNE also keeps species information (94% vs 60% for UMAP), so figures use t-SNE. On a t-SNE map, which photos sit together is reliable; distances, positions and sizes of groups are not. Its use is to find photos inside another organ's group: 262 for EfficientNet (16%), most often fruit among inflorescence (28), inflorescence among fruit (25), leaf among whole tree (18). These may be unusual shots, label errors or multi-organ photos; the list is exported for manual review.

Interpretation. A 3-D PCA plot loses 13%–32% of organ information and keeps fewer than 30% of neighbour relations, so it cannot be used to judge organ structure or clusters. 64-D PCA keeps organ, scale and species information almost completely: all further analysis runs in 64 dimensions. Display figures use 2-D t-SNE: its grouping is reliable, but distances, cluster sizes and positions carry no meaning.

Method. Each photo is a high-dimensional vector (EfficientNet 1,280, BioCLIP 1,024, DINOv3 768, YOLO 512 / 896). For each reduction we measure:
Neighbours kept: of each photo's 15 most similar photos in the full space, how many remain;
Information kept: nearest-neighbour vote for organ / scale / species in the reduced space (cross-validated, grouped by plant), as a percentage of the full-space accuracy; 100% = nothing lost.
Also how much of each principal component's variation is explained by organ / scale / species (η², 0–1). All reductions are unsupervised; labels are used only to evaluate. Procedure. PCA to 2 / 3 / 16 / 64 dimensions and 2-D t-SNE (five models); UMAP to 2 / 16 dimensions (EfficientNet).

2 · Choice of K and soft clustering

Groupings are most stable and organ-aligned at K = 5–7; about 32% of photos lie between two groups

Select the number of clusters K with numerical criteria, and identify photos lying between two groups with soft membership.

modelK=3 matches scaleK=7 matches organstability K=3stability K=7stability K=20
EfficientNet-B00.800.680.660.720.52
BioCLIP 2.50.440.290.840.550.48
DINOv30.770.580.630.700.55

EfficientNet K=7: 32% of photos are ambiguous (533), repeatably (two independent halves correlate 0.84). Most often between:

between which two organsnshare of ambiguousof which both plausible
fruit ↔ twig1560.2972
leaf ↔ leaf920.170
inflorescence ↔ leaf660.1218
fruit ↔ whole tree570.1132
inflorescence ↔ twig560.1118

Example: photos between fruit ↔ twig

Interpretation. K=3 corresponds to shot scale, K=7 to organ; K=20 has no basis. The ambiguity is real and repeatable, mostly between neighbouring organs (fruit ↔ twig, inflorescence ↔ leaf), but it does not predict species errors.

Method. K is a choice; we use meaningful values: K=3 (three shot scales), K=7 (seven organs), K=20 (old default). Do groups match labels one-to-one, and are they stable when plants are resampled?
Soft membership: resample plants 50 times and recluster; the share of runs a photo lands in each group is its membership. Max membership <0.8 = ambiguous. Procedure. First version (Gaussian mixture) said almost no photo is ambiguous. On review this was a dimension artefact: same data, 22% ambiguous in 2-D, 1% in 32-D. Withdrawn and replaced by resampling.

3 · Group composition: enrichment analysis

General vision models group photos by organ; BioCLIP groups them by species

Quantify the organ, shot-scale and species make-up of each group and determine what drives it.

modelK=7 groups dominated by one organmedian top-species share
EfficientNet-B00.860.07
BioCLIP 2.50.140.17
DINOv30.710.07
YOLO11s backbone0.290.07
YOLO11s neck0.290.07

Interpretation. EfficientNet (86%) and DINOv3 (71%) groups are mostly dominated by one organ and are not single-species groups; BioCLIP (14%) groups follow species; YOLO about a third.

Method. For every group: share of each organ / scale relative to the overall rate (fold enrichment), adjusted for species mix, with intervals from resampling plants. Photos are nested in plants and species, so independence fails: effect sizes only, no p-values. Procedure. Five models × K = 3 / 7 / 20.

4 · Dimensions that define the groups: shrunken centroids (NSC)

Only EfficientNet concentrates organ information in few dimensions (about 8 per class)

Find the fewest dimensions needed to separate organs and to reproduce the clusters, as a measure of how concentrated the information is.

modelorgan: coords keptorgan: per classorgan: accuracy keptgrouping K=3grouping K=7grouping K=20
EfficientNet-B0227.860.97382064
BioCLIP 2.56452.430.9836464
DINOv36437.570.96143462
YOLO11s backbone6450.140.98264664
YOLO11s neck6448.710.9884864

Reading: to the right = fewer coordinates; y = accuracy relative to all coordinates; dot = chosen Δ. Flat then a cliff = concentrated; sliding from the start = spread out.

EfficientNet: which directions identify each organ (red / blue = the two ends, white = not used).

Interpretation. Only EfficientNet compresses organ to ~8 coordinates per class with almost no loss; elsewhere organ information is spread out. Coordinates needed to reproduce the groups grow with K; "almost all 64" was a K=20 effect.

Method. NSC (nearest shrunken centroids): a centre per class and its deviation on every coordinate; Δ is a threshold, coordinates deviating less than Δ are dropped for that class. Δ=0 keeps all; larger Δ is sparser. Δ chosen by 5-fold CV grouped by plant and the one-standard-error rule (sparsest model statistically as good as the best); test set used once. Coordinates are PCA directions, not biological traits. Procedure. Two tasks: (a) external organ labels; (b) reproducing the model's own K = 3 / 7 / 20 groups. Five models.

An autoencoder does not improve on PCA; the first principal component is camera distance

EfficientNet PC1, both ends (correlation with shot scale ρ = -0.65):

Interpretation. The AE matches PCA on error and is worse on neighbours: no gain from non-linearity, line closed. The first axis is camera distance: close-up leaves at one end, distant whole trees at the other.

Method. A 32-D autoencoder vs PCA on reconstruction error and neighbour retention; then real photos at both ends of each principal axis and its correlation with shot scale and organ. Procedure. AE results recovered from the previous site and checked with a linear AE (matches PCA, so code and data line up).

6 · Back from the latent space to images

Group centres can be shown with real photos; heatmaps are faithful to the model, alignment with organs is untested

Map points in the latent space back to real photos, and locate the image regions the model relies on with activation maps.

modelK3 retrieved = dominant organK7 retrieved = dominant organK20 retrieved = dominant organ
EfficientNet-B00.940.900.90
BioCLIP 2.50.560.550.59
DINOv30.721.000.92

Nearest real photos to two group centres:

Grad-CAM (earlier K=20 run): red = relied on most.

Interpretation. Retrieval shows what each group looks like (its most typical members, so groups look tidier than they are). Heatmaps are faithful to the model, but whether they land on the organ is not yet tested; that needs organ masks.

Method. Inversion: for each group centre, retrieve the most similar real photos. Heatmaps: Grad-CAM on EfficientNet (a CNN like ResNet) with "belongs to group c" as the target, checked by occlusion. Procedure. Generating images from noise (previous round) gave coloured noise; replaced by retrieval. Heatmaps on 80 rule-sampled photos: hiding the hot area hurts the score more than a random area in 88% of cases.

7 · Multiple labels per image

Soft clustering shortlists 181 photos that may contain several organs, as candidates for multi-label annotation

Use soft-clustering results to shortlist photos that may contain several organs and need multi-label annotation.

Interpretation. The candidate list is ready for annotation; confirming two organs in the frame needs the multi-label data (Human Gold / Gemma multi-label) exported.

Method. Organ labels are single-label today. In soft clustering, a photo in its own organ's group whose second candidate is another organ is marked "both organs plausible": a multi-label candidate. Procedure. EfficientNet K=7: 181 candidates (34% of ambiguous photos).

8 · YOLO comparison (team direction)

Off-the-shelf YOLO embeddings carry the least organ information and need training on organ labels

Assess whether YOLO whole-image embeddings support organ-structure analysis, to inform the decision on switching to YOLO.

modelorgan F1species F1NSC organ coords / classK=7 organ-dominated groups
EfficientNet-B00.650.107.860.86
BioCLIP 2.50.720.7952.430.14
DINOv30.830.4337.570.71
YOLO11s backbone0.600.0950.140.29
YOLO11s neck0.620.0748.710.29

Interpretation. YOLO carries the least organ information (organ F1: backbone 0.60, neck 0.62) and cannot be compressed; its groups have clear structure, but not by organ. If we switch to YOLO, it needs training on our organ labels; raw embeddings are not enough. This says nothing about YOLO's box detection after training.

Method. Whole-image embeddings of YOLO11s (COCO general detector, not trained on plants), two versions: backbone (512-D) and multi-scale neck (896-D), run through the same analyses as the other models. Procedure. Organ / species probes, NSC, group make-up, retrieval.

Next steps

Decisions and follow-up

Proposed decisions

  1. Use 64-D PCA as the analysis space; t-SNE for display.
  2. Use K = 5–7 (matches the number of organs, most stable).
  3. Use DINOv3 / EfficientNet for organ structure and BioCLIP for species.
  4. Train YOLO on organ labels before including it in the same analyses.

Follow-up work

  1. Export multi-label organ data (Human Gold) and verify the "both plausible" candidates.
  2. Build organ masks to test whether heatmaps land on the organ.
  3. If YOLO is adopted: fine-tune on organ boxes, then rerun the same analyses.
  4. Re-test the conclusions on external Pound Ridge field photos.
